headline: Intra-African Trade Loses $5 Billion Annually to Payment Delays and Fees
summary: Banking settlement delays and intermediary currency routing fees cost Africa an estimated $5 billion per year. Most intra-African commercial transactions are routed through extra-continental correspondent banks.
why: High cross-border friction limits the implementation and economic benefits of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

impacts.name: African Trade
impacts.why: Higher settlement transaction costs reduce cross-border regional commerce margins.
